Lab 023 · Lesson 023 · simulation using the lesson's numbers

GPU Pipeline Lab

The GPU is an assembly line of four stations. The busiest one sets the GPU time. Pull one lever at a time and watch which bar is red, and whether the GPU time moves at all.

Coral Garden, mid-range phone. Goal: GPU at most 28 ms, at 100% render scale, with a real shader (not the flat test one).

Not yet

The assembly line

GPU time0ms
Frame rate0fps
LimiterPixelbusy
Budget left0ms of 28
Coral trianglesvertex station
Render scale1600×720
Pixel shaderpixel station
Colour formatmemory station
Fish in the shoalvertex station

Each layer: about +4 ms memory and +1 ms pixel at 100%, 8-byte colour.

Four-lever test

From the current settings, pull one lever, read the GPU time, put it back. The lever that moves the GPU time points at the limiter. The marked row is the biggest drop from a lever that unloads only one station.

What the GPU tool says

A counter capture in the style of Xcode, Streamline or Snapdragon Profiler: each station's load and how busy it is. Busy % = load ÷ GPU time.

Lesson 023 · The Coral Garden

    
    
  
    

  
    
    
    What this shows
    
    
    
      
    The slowest station sets the pace
    GPU time ≈ fixed work + the biggest station load. Speeding up any other station gains 0 ms, like halving the coral triangles.
    
      
    One lever, one question
    Each lever unloads one station. The resolution test says "per-pixel"; the shader and format levers say which station.
    
      
    The bottleneck moves
    After the fix, memory is next in line. The 4-byte format did nothing at first and becomes a real fix once murk layers arrive. Budget each station.
    
    
    
    
    This lab is a simulation, not a measurement. Loads come from Lesson 023: fixed work 3 ms; vertex 6 ms for the coral and 3 ms for 400 fish; raster 2 ms per 9 ms of vertex work plus 2 ms for the pixels; pixel 38 ms (live caustics), 22 ms (baked) or 6 ms (flat), plus 1 ms per murk layer; memory 15 ms plus 4 ms per murk layer at 8 bytes per pixel. Per-pixel work scales with the number of pixels. CPU work is 14 ms and the game caps at 30 fps. Real GPUs share shader cores between stations and overlap less perfectly, so a station that is not the limiter can still move the total a little.
